q-94486.name: Question 1
q-94486.problem: What is the trace in the $yz$-plane of the elliptic cone $\frac{3{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}={z}^{2}\,?$
q-94486.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $yz$-plane, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{0}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & ={z}^{2} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & ={z}^{2} \\ z & =\pm \frac{y}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two lines in the $yz$-plane with equations $z=\pm \frac{y}{3}.$

 z=±y9+1
b
 z=±y3
c
 z=−y3
d
 z=±y9
e
 z=−y3±1
Submit

024+y29=z2y29=z2z=±y3

q-94496.name: Question 2
q-94496.problem: What is the trace in the $xy$-plane of the elliptic cone $9(x-2)^{2}+2{y}^{2}=18{z}^{2}\,?$
q-94496.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xy$-plane, we substitute $z=0$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9(x-2)^{2}+2{y}^{2}=18(0)^{2} \\ 9(x-2)^{2}+2{y}^{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

This gives in the $xy$-plane the point $(2,0,0).$

q-94699.name: Question 3
q-94699.problem: Find the center of the elliptic cone $8(x-6)^{2}+12(y-4)^{2}=4(z+2)^{2}.$
q-94699.worked_solution:
The general equation of an elliptic cone with center at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is

$$
\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=\frac{(z-{z}_{0})^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

To find the center, we rewrite our equation in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}8(x-6)^{2}+12(y-4)^{2} & =4(z+2)^{2} \\ \frac{(x-6)^{2}}{1/8}+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{1/12} & =\frac{(z+2)^{2}}{1/4} \\ \frac{(x-6)^{2}}{1/8}+\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{1/12} & =\frac{(z-(-2))^{2}}{1/4}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic cone that has its center at $(6,4,-2).$

Find the center of the elliptic cone 8(x−6)2+12(y−4)2=4(z+2)2.

a
 (−6,−4,2)
b
(6,4,−2)
c
(2,3,−1)
d
(8,12,4)
e
(−2,−3,1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The general equation of an elliptic cone with center at the point (x0,y0,z0) is

(x−x0)2a2+(y−y0)2b2=(z−z0)2c2.

To find the center, we rewrite our equation in standard form, as follows:

8(x−6)2+12(y−4)2=4(z+2)2(x−6)21/8+(y−4)21/12=(z+2)21/4(x−6)21/8+(y−4)21/12=(z−(−2))21/4

This gives us the equation of an elliptic cone that has its center at (6,4,−2).
